summary: Ninini Point light, Kauai: a fixed white light from 1897 on an open wooden tower; the 72-foot concrete tower dates from 1932.

structures.note: Forty feet tall (LighthouseFriends); lamp room 70 ft above the sea (1897 notice).
72-foot tower completed by contract; the archive gives 1933.

events.note: Fixed white light at Ninini point, north of the entrance to Nawiliwili bay (notice dated Honolulu 18 Oct 1897).
Open wooden frame tower with enclosed lamp room, painted white; site leased by the Hawaiian government from Lihue Plantation.
Federal lighthouse administration of the Hawaiian lights begins; lamp room replaced by a small box carrying a lens lantern.
Old tower torn down; 33.5-foot mast with lens lantern first exhibited 22 Dec 1906; oil-wick light 'established' 1906 per the 1933 bulletin.
Lighthouse Service asks Congress for $22,000 for a 72-foot reinforced concrete tower (as reported by LighthouseFriends).
36-inch revolving airways beacon installed on a temporary 40-foot wooden tower, 21 July 1931.
Permanent 72-foot reinforced concrete tower completed by contract; the light moved to it 15 Nov 1932 (archive gives 1933).
Automated 1953; an attendant stayed on for routine maintenance of this light and seven minor lights on the island (LighthouseFriends).

corrections.proposed: open wooden frame tower, built 1897 (about 12 m); reinforced concrete tower, built 1932, 22 m (72 ft)
corrections.why: The 1897 notice describes an open wooden frame tower, and LighthouseFriends gives the first tower as forty feet. The concrete tower was completed by contract and the light moved to it on 15 November 1932 (Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1933, p. 6). The 24.5 m height has no source among those read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The roster gives 1917 to 1938; LighthouseFriends says he was assigned to the light in 1918 and retired in 1939, when the Coast Guard took control. The story gives both and does not choose between them.
LighthouseFriends says the light was automated in 1953 with an attendant kept on; the archive roster lists keepers to at least 1971. The story states both and does not settle the difference.

The 1897 notice confirms a fixed white light at Ninini point, so 1897 stands. The archive's 1904 is the year federal administration began (Bulletin 1936 p. 37; LighthouseFriends). The oil light the 1933 bulletin calls 'established' in 1906 and the mast first exhibited 22 Dec 1906 are later lights on the same point.

The 1933 bulletin (p. 6) says the concrete tower was completed by contract and the light moved to it on 15 November 1932; the 1932 bulletin (p. 36) says it was still nearing completion that year. The archive's Year Tower Established is 1933, and Rowlett's directory gives 1933 for 'Tower 3'. The story follows the contemporary bulletin and gives the archive's date.
The roster names John McLaughlin; LighthouseFriends' narrative calls him James McLaughlin. Roster spelling kept; first name unresolved.

notes_for_editor: Roster matched by name ('nawiliwili-harbor'); its USLHS position is 11 km from the station, and the archive's coordinates (21 deg 51'20" N) are wrong for the point; the 1897 notice's 21 deg 57' N fits the record. Roster lines are used as printed, with person slugs from roster.py. LighthouseFriends narrative (Souza's marriage and 1902 letter, the McLaughlin anecdote, the 1929 request) is secondary and was not checked against Hawaii State Archives. The 1897 notice's issuing office is cut off in the OCR. The record's focal height 33.5 m (ENC) may echo the 33.5-foot 1906 mast (LighthouseFriends); current optics and characteristic (Fl W 15s, ENC) were not verified. The record's 'concrete tower built 1897, 24.5 m' is not supported by any source read. No wreck, storm or rescue at Ninini Point appeared in the sources read; the Garden Island (Lihue) and Hawaiian Gazette were searched only lightly. The 1933 Bulletin's text is OCR-damaged; quotations were copied as read, and the 1933 p. 6 sentence on the 1932 completion is partly garbled. Visit access follows LighthouseFriends (grounds open, tower closed); the record's open-to-public flag is from the archive.
